chunks: And from him, from Humayd, from al-Hasan ibn Sam'ah, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding a man who has a female servant, and she uncovers herself so he sees her, or he strips her, without going beyond that, he said: 'It is not permissible for his son [to marry her].'
ai.seo_question: Does a father seeing or stripping his female servant prevent his son from marrying her?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the specific condition of 'seeing' or 'stripping' (*tajrid*) as insufficient to establish a permanent marital prohibition (*mahram*) between a father and his concubine for his son. In Shia jurisprudence, this distinguishes mere visual or partial exposure from full sexual consummation, which is typically required to create the barrier to marriage, thereby allowing the son to marry the same concubine after her manumission.
